surface/mcp/instructions.why: The MCP instructions lead with the cheap way to write cases (coverage, case_new, map_plan, then driving) and with case_impact after a code change; a trial agent never found those tools from the old text. The FastSim paragraph says a FastSim bundle is a release bundle, so the app must call qa.register outside if (__DEV__); a trial agent registered its commands behind __DEV__ and they were missing on FastSim.

surface/commands.why: fastsim start and fastsim stop: a FastSim host for a session or an MCP server to explore on

surface/help/fastsim start.why: new command: starts a FastSim host on the session's driver port

surface/help/fastsim stop.why: new command: stops the host fastsim start started

surface/mcp/full.why: fastsim_start and fastsim_stop are served over MCP

surface/mcp/tool/fastsim_start.why: new tool: explore the app on a FastSim host

surface/mcp/tool/fastsim_stop.why: new tool: stops the host fastsim_start started

surface/usage.why: the usage lists fastsim start and fastsim stop

report/answer.why: A failed case's summary now opens with the failing step's own error (— failed at: <step>), which it used to leave out when the evidence explained nothing.

surface/help/case stop.why: case stop is new: it stops a case run that is going, from a terminal or over MCP (case_stop).

surface/mcp/tool/case_stop.why: case_stop is a new MCP tool, so a model can stop a case_run its client moved to the background.

wire/press-by-number.why: A failed case reads its reasons from the trace since the case's first step (trace since), not the whole trace, so an older failure is not given as its cause.

surface/help/case run.why: --jobs and --host-command no longer need --ports: free driver ports are picked when none are given, as the FastSim guide promised.

wire/failure-stops-and-tears-down.why: a failed app.press reads the screen once more, to name a native view outside React Native that covers the app (the Expo dev menu's onboarding sheet) instead of leaving only ~covered.

wire/compare-run-frames.why: Every case now clears the app's netmock rules before its first step (and after its last when it set one), so a mock left by an earlier case or by hand never answers for this one. With screenshots, an action step reads the commit count first and the frame waits for a commit past it (idle after), so a press frame no longer shows the screen from before the press.
